newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares fall victim to weak forex, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German shares fall victim to weak forex, Wall St.

text.p: German shares took fright at currency turbulence and U.S. market weakness on Friday as a touch of pre-weekend catharsis hit sentiment on the stock exchange.
The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 60.20 points, or 1.36 percent, at 4,354.15 points.
The descent steepened in the afternoon, with the IBIS DAX index ended a jittery session down nearly two percent at 4,342.31 points. September DTB DAX futures fell 100 to 4,345.0.
Late afternoon trade saw the dollar slide below 1.85 marks amid sharp losses on sterling, while the Dow Jones index started out with significant losses.
Many dealers, taken aback at the pace of the share market decline, said the move was overdone.
Losses were spread across the board, with the only exceptions in the financial sector, where Commerzbank, buoyed all day on a wave of takeover talk, continued to thrive in the afternoon session.
Selected bank shares had outperformed through the day amid a fresh wave of takeover speculation which most dealers dismissed as idle chatter.
The speculation nonetheless pushed financials ahead as the so-called "silly season", when rumours fly as many market players are away on holiday, started in earnest.
Commerzbank AG led volumes and traded ahead against the trend to end the bourse session at 66.55 marks, up 3.10 marks or 4.89 percent.
Various buyers were being mooted for Commerzbank, including the large Swiss banks, rival Deutsche Bank and HSBC.
Dresdner Bank was also up 50 pfennigs at 81.20 marks and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG was up 1.40 marks at 98.10 marks.
Dealers were mainly unfazed by the weakness of prices, saying this was typical of the end to a slow week.
The highlights for next week would be interim results for the chemical sector, which will kick off on Tuesday with a report from Henkel.
